q: What is the difference between insetting and offsetting?
title: Insetting vs offsetting
short: Insetting means funding reductions inside your own value chain, such as helping a supplier switch fuel; they show up as lower Scope 3 when the supplier's data changes. Offsetting means buying credits from outside it, reported separately and never subtracted from your inventory.

ul: Counts only through measured lower emissions in your supplier data.
Paying for a project does not by itself change your figures.
Credits are retired and reported alongside, not deducted.
Check the credit's quality, for example against ICVCM principles.

p: Insetting is not a GHG Protocol term. Describe what you funded and what changed in the data.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.
